title: Adaptive Federated Learning for Privacy-Preserving Smart Applications
authors: Dominguez, B.L.; Emmanuel, R.; Montemayor, A.F.
tldr: An adaptive federated learning framework improves convergence speed and privacy by dynamically adjusting aggregation strategies and incorporating differential privacy mechanisms.
problem_and_motivation: Traditional federated learning approaches struggle with heterogeneous data distributions, limited device resources, and dynamic network conditions, leading to degraded model performance. Privacy-preserving mechanisms often introduce trade-offs between model accuracy and security. There is a need for a framework that balances adaptivity, performance, and privacy in smart applications.
approach: Proposed an Adaptive Federated Learning (AFL) framework with dynamic aggregation strategies based on client performance metrics and resource availability.
Integrated differential privacy mechanisms and secure aggregation to ensure robust privacy guarantees without compromising model accuracy.
Evaluated AFL on benchmark smart application datasets including IoT sensor data and mobile user behavior logs.
Compared AFL to FedAvg and FedProx baselines using metrics of accuracy, convergence speed, communication overhead, and privacy leakage risk.
Designed communication optimization through dynamic client participation and update compression techniques.
findings: num: AFL achieved 92.3% accuracy on HAR dataset versus 84.7% for FedAvg and 87.5% for FedProx.
num: AFL showed up to 28% reduction in communication overhead compared to FedAvg.
num: Membership inference attack success rates reduced to 18.4% with AFL versus 42.1% for FedAvg.
num: Active clients per round dropped by approximately 20% without harming accuracy.
num: Performance loss from differential privacy noise remained below 2%.
key_figures_tables: Table 1: Comparison of model accuracy and convergence speed across HAR, FEMNIST, and OpenIoT datasets → AFL outperforms baselines in all metrics.
Figure 2: Communication efficiency comparison → AFL demonstrates significant bandwidth reduction.
Figure 3: Membership inference attack success rate → AFL provides stronger privacy protection.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper contributes an adaptive federated learning framework that dynamically adjusts aggregation strategies based on client performance and resource availability. It integrates differential privacy and secure aggregation to provide strong privacy guarantees while maintaining model accuracy. The framework demonstrates improvements in convergence speed and communication efficiency compared to standard federated learning methods. The work advances the understanding of balancing adaptivity, performance, and privacy in distributed machine learning systems.
directly_justifies: Adaptive weighting based on data quality and performance reduces client drift in non-IID settings.
Integration of differential privacy and secure aggregation provides robust privacy protection.
Dynamic client participation improves communication efficiency without sacrificing accuracy.
limits: Evaluation limited to specific benchmark datasets (HAR, FEMNIST, OpenIoT).
Computational overhead of adaptive mechanisms may require optimization for large-scale deployments.
Privacy-accuracy trade-off requires careful tuning based on application requirements.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scan of all topic domains identified high relevance for data privacy and security (10.A) and on-device vs. server inference (14.C) due to core focus on privacy-preserving distributed learning. Medium relevance for ML model serving and deployment (14.B) due to discussion of federated model training. Low relevance for financial behavioral profiles (5.A) and predictive modeling (6.A) as finance is mentioned but not central. Contextual relevance for landscape of existing systems (4.A) as provides background on privacy challenges. Domains related to budgeting, expense categorization, and engagement were considered and rejected as not covered by this federated learning paper.
